notes: Only one new core (Calgary CHGI 2025 internal list) gave a usable 6000-vs-X pair with output Gb listed. Salk, Rush, UCLA, UConn, CWRU, TGen and Dana-Farber were already covered or priced only the X. CWRU (updated 07/2026) lists only the X 10B/25B, and no 6000 appears. That fits the 6000 being phased out at that core. The UNMC pricing page returned 404 and its search snippet was a stale July 2023 page. Bonn and other candidates were not reached. Rush June 2026 lists S4 2x150 at $6,615 and S2 1x100 at $4,880 with the unit unclear. Both are internal rates and can't be turned into a reliable $/Gb. Overall the result is thin: 1 usable core against a target of 5, and the Calgary 25B is a partner-run lane, so the comparison is only loosely like-for-like.
how_to_mine: Find 2025-26 PDFs or HTML rate cards that give output Gb next to price for both platforms. Calgary-style 'Output Gbp' columns are ideal. Try the Rush GMCF June 2026 PDF to confirm whether S4 $6,615 is per lane or per flow cell, then compute $/Gb using about 750 Gb per S4 lane. Try Salk's omics rates page for dated 2026 values. Search for 'NovaSeq 6000' alongside '25B' on Bonn, Penn, MDC Berlin, Michigan State RTSF, Illinois Roy J. Carver, UGA and UT Austin GSAF. Compare year over year to see whether 6000 prices have stayed flat while X prices fell.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: At Calgary's core in 2025, the NovaSeq 6000 S4 cost about 1.6-1.7x the NovaSeq X 25B per Gb.
items.detail: Calgary CHGI 2025 internal list: S4 v1.5 300-cycle flow cell $22,420 for 3,000 Gb gives $7.47/Gb. The S4 single lane is $5,820 for 750 Gb, or $7.76/Gb. The NovaSeq X 25B lane (300 cycles) is $4,100 for 900 Gb, or $4.56/Gb. The ratio is 1.64x for the flow cell and 1.70x for the lane, well below the roughly 3.4x ratio in Illumina's revenue per Gb. At core level the 6000 premium is smaller, which suggests the 41%-of-revenue skew comes from list-price and discount structure at clinical and large accounts.
items.source_name: University of Calgary Centre for Health Genomics and Informatics, Internal Price List 2025
items.why_new: Gives a same-sheet 6000 vs X $/Gb ratio (1.6-1.7x) from the Gb column. Prior notes had Calgary only as a source name and had no per-Gb ratio.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: The core-level 6000 premium over the X is far smaller than the roughly 3.4x in Illumina's reported revenue per Gb.
items.detail: Calgary's 25B lane is a partner-run (BC Genome Sequencing Centre) lane with a longer turnaround and no custom primers. This makes it a discounted tier, so the ratio may be understated. The X 25B at $4.56/Gb is also above the roughly $2.5-3.0/Gb seen at other cores. So 1.6-1.7x is a lower bound for the premium. The 41%/17% skew probably reflects clinical or large-account pricing rather than academic core rates.
items.why_new: Quantifies a watch-out: core user prices do not reproduce the 3.4x gap, so the gap must come from the customer mix.
